attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. 'I don't believe' is a firm statement of his view, not a hedge.

semantics.note: Matches the sentence. In context, though, 'viable' means capacity that is already built and big enough for OpenAI's expansion. The same passage covers CoreWeave and OpenAI taking up the $12bn CoreWeave option.

contract.note: The contradiction condition counts any signed non-Microsoft deal, but the speaker openly named those deals in the same passage. His point was that existing capacity outside Microsoft was not enough for OpenAI's expansion. That reading is stretched against him and ignores the 'existing' qualifier.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own release, dated March 2025: an $11.9bn contract for future delivery, with Altman naming Oracle deals. It shows deals were signed, not that enough existing capacity was usable, which the post already admits.
Oracle release from 2024, before the target period. It describes OCI as an extension of Microsoft's Azure, not a source independent of Microsoft.
Reuters report from July 2025: Azure was exclusive until January, and OpenAI relies on Oracle and CoreWeave. It gives no amounts of capacity in use before mid-April.

reviews.rationale: On a fair reading (existing capacity outside Microsoft that is big enough for OpenAI's expansion), the packet shows deals were signed but has no data on capacity delivered. The packet admits this gap. The contract's 'any arrangement' test is unfair to words that already acknowledged those arrangements. So the outcome is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm 'will' conditional with no deadline, joined to a present-tense judgment about room to expand. The antecedent is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'at this rate' as strong continued growth is an ordinary reading. Splitting the claim into two parts, with an early-resolution rule for each, follows how the claim is built. Judging 'room to expand' by later deals is acceptable because the sentence looks forward.

evidence.note: Supports the antecedent only: weekly users rose from 500M in March to 800M in October 2025, so growth continued.
August 2025: Altman described rationing compute and a ceiling on API growth after GPT-5's launch, a capacity problem matching part (a). The source is the CEO's own statement as reported.
Amazon release, November 2025: a $38bn AWS deal giving OpenAI hundreds of thousands of GPUs, which shows large room to expand. This is a company disclosure.
Altman said OpenAI would roughly double its compute fleet within five months. This is a company claim and was not independently verified.

reviews.rationale: Growth continued, so the antecedent was met. Part (a) holds: in August 2025 OpenAI described rationing compute because of capacity limits. Part (b) fails: OpenAI signed a $38bn AWS deal and said it would roughly double its fleet, so it had substantial room to expand. Dated events settle both parts under the contract's rule.
